metadata.title: Revisiting Time-Aware Approaches for Code Technical Debt Prediction: A Bayesian Exploration - Replication Package (SANER 2026 RENE Track)
metadata.description:
This is a replication package and online appendix for our paper submitted to the SANER 2026 Reproducibility Studies and Negative Results (RENE) Track: "Revisiting Time-Aware Approaches for Code Technical Debt Prediction: A Bayesian Exploration".

NOTE: All the file hyperlinks included into this README will not work within the Zenodo description, but only once the reader downloads the registration package.

Overview

This package focuses on technical debt prediction through Bayesian analysis, examining how different models and estimators can effectively forecast technical debt in software projects.The primary objective of this research is to assess the reliability and effectiveness of various Bayesian models in predicting Code Technical Debt(TD), drawing on historical data from the Technical Debt Dataset. By investigating the application of these models across different project datasets, this study aims to offer developers and project managers predictive tools for better decision-making in managing software quality.

Prerequisites & Installation

For installation and more insights on the prerequisites to replicate our study, please go over instructions in INSTALL.md.

Scripts

  • scripts/: Python scripts for time-series/Bayesian modeling, preprocessing, and orchestration.

    • bayesian_prediction_orbit_DLT.py: Bayesian forecasting with Orbit DLT (Dynamic Linear Trend) model.
    • bayesian_prediction_orbit_ETS.py: Exponential smoothing-like forecasting with Orbit ETS model.
    • bayesian_prediction_pyDLM.py: Bayesian Dynamic Linear Models with pyDLM.
    • bayesian_pybats_dglm.py: PyBATS Dynamic Generalized Linear Models (count/GLM-family).
    • commons.py: Shared constants, paths, and helper utilities.
    • main.py: Pipeline entry point: orchestrates prep → modeling → export.
    • merge_results.py: Merges per-model outputs into consolidated results.
    • modules.py: Reusable components (model wrappers, helpers).
    • preprocessing.py: Data cleaning and feature engineering routines.
    • tsDataPreparation.py: Time-series preparation (resampling, seasonality, splits).

Data

  • data/: Main folder containing all datasets and experiment results.

    • raw-data/: Contains the foundational raw datasets used for the analysis.

      • multivariate_data.csv: Core multivariate dataset combining several metrics.
      • commits.csv: Commit-level metadata and version control data.
      • issues.csv: Issue-tracking data (e.g., bug reports, tasks, or defects).

    • monthly_data/: Monthly-level datasets for each analyzed project.
      Each CSV corresponds to a single Apache project’s evolution and refactoring metrics across time.

      • digester.csv
      • commons-fileupload.csv
      • zookeeper.csv
      • hive.csv
      • httpclient.csv
      • (...and many others such as beanutils.csv, felix.csv, batik.csv, etc.)

    • results/: Contains all computed model results and statistical outputs.

      • HP_results/: Results from statistical tests or high-performance analyses.

        • BiWeekly-WC.jmp
        • Monthly-WC.jmp
        • BiWeekly-Dunn.jmp
        • monthly_AD.jmp
        • (These .jmp files are outputs from JMP statistical software and store test results for various time granularities.)

      • global_results/: Aggregated experiment outcomes combining all projects.

        • global_results.csv: Overall combined dataset.
        • global_results_monthly.csv: Monthly-level global results.
        • global_results_biweekly.csv: Bi-weekly aggregated results.

      • model_based_results/: Results of Bayesian and statistical model analyses.

        • ORBIT_ML_DLT_Result/: Main output folder from Bayesian modeling pipelines.

          • complete/Results/:
            Contains the main outputs of Bayesian models and their diagnostic metrics.

            • linear_stan-map_assesment.csv
            • loglinear_stan-mcmc_assesment.csv
            • linear_stan-mcmc_assesment.csv
            • loglinear_stan-map_assesment.csv
              → These files summarize Bayesian model fit quality and inference outcomes.

          • complete/Confidence Intervals/:
            Contains confidence interval computations per project and model type.

            • zookeeper_loglinear_stan-mcmc_confidence_intervals.csv
            • httpclient_linear_stan-mcmc_confidence_intervals.csv
            • digester_linear_stan-map_confidence_intervals.csv
            • commons-fileupload_loglinear_stan-map_confidence_intervals.csv
            • ognl_loglinear_stan-map_confidence_intervals.csv
            • (Additional files exist for multiple other projects.)

License

All datasets are released under the Creative Commons 4.0 Attribution License (CC BY 4.0).
All scripts and modeling code are released under the MIT License.

Each analyzed software project must comply with its respective open-source license as distributed within its repository.

Notes

  • The .csv files are ready-to-analyze tabular datasets used for statistical inference.
  • The .jmp files are outputs from the JMP statistical software for replicating the results shown in the manuscript.
  • The repository structure ensures reproducibility across raw data, aggregated metrics, and model-based inference outputs.

metadata.title: Replication Package for: Evaluating LLMs on Medical Diagnostics Leveraging a Golden Model & Combinatorial Testing
metadata.description:
Replication package for: "Evaluating LLMs on Medical Diagnostics Leveraging a Golden Model & Combinatorial Testing", which is an extenstion to [5, 6, 7]. This package provides the data retrieved during experiments for the corresponding paper. The experiments are performed using ChatGPT[1] and GPT-4o[2,3] which are evaluated against NetDoktor's "Symptom-Checker"[4]. Furthermore, it should be noted that these models are closed-source and might be updated by the vendors at any time. Because of this and the non-deterministic nature of LLMs results might differ on re-runs of the experiments. Finally, we provide the code for aggregating data from [4], so that it can be leveraged as a golden model.

[1] OpenAI(2023). ChatGPT. Online: chat.openai.com/chat.
[2] OpenAI (2023). GPT-4 technical report. In arXiv: 2303.08774. arXiv.
[3] OpenAI (2024). Introducing GPT-4o and more tools to ChatGPT free users. Online: https://openai.com/index/gpt-4o-and-more-tools-to-chatgpt-free.
[4] Richter et al. (2024). Symptom-Checker. Online: www.netdoktor.at/symptom-checker.
[5] Perko et al. (2024). Testing ChatGPT's Performance on Medical Diagnostic Tasks.
[6] Perko et al. (2024). Using Combinatorial Testing for Prompt Engineering of LLMs in Medicine.
[7] Mujic et al. (2025). Extraction of Knowledge Representations for Reasoning from Medical Questionnaires.

metadata.title: Replication package of "Automation and Reuse Practices in GitHub Actions Workflows: A Practitioner's Perspective"
metadata.description:
This is the replication package of the paper "Automation and Reuse Practices in GitHub Actions Workflows: A Practitioner’s Perspective" by Hassan Onsori Delicheh, Guillaume Cardoen, Alexandre Decan and Tom Mens (Software Engineering Lab, University of Mons, Belgium). This paper presents a survey amongst GitHub Actions practitionners to understands the automation and reuse practices used in GitHub Actions workflows.

This replication package is composed of multiple Jupyter notebooks, reproducing every results presented in the paper. The file requirements.txt contains every needed dependencies to run these Jupyter notebooks, and README.md provides common commands for installing the requirements.

Note that these notebooks requires the anonymized responses of the survey, which can be found on Zenodo.

metadata.title: SQuaD: The Software Quality Dataset - Replication Package
metadata.description:
This is a replication package and online appendix for the MSR 2026 Data and Tool Showcase Track paper: "SQuaD: The Software Quality Dataset".

NOTE: All the file hyperlinks included into this README will not work within the Zenodo description, but only once the reader downloads the registration package.

Contents

This repository contains the following:

  • INSTALL: Detailed installation instructions for each of the used tools as well as the required Python dependencies.

  • Figures: Graphical content shared in the manuscript.

    • mining-pipeline.pdf: Overview of the dataset construction methodology.
    • entity-relationship-diagram.pdf: Enhanced Entity-Relationship (EER) diagram of the created dataset.

Datasets

  • Official Dataset Zenodo page: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17566690
  • CSV Raw Data (IDA Storage): https://doi.org/10.23729/fd-c528d131-2c8c-3e61-91f1-a075931e73dc
  • MongoDB BSON (IDA Storage): https://doi.org/10.23729/fd-f9dc7d2c-0465-3991-961f-56128ee518d0

Scripts

  • msr-dataset/: Main project folder containing the full data mining and merging pipeline.

    • tool_mining/: Main repository containing all scripts and batch jobs for mining, analyzing, and summarizing software repositories.

      • batch_jobs/: Contains shell scripts for automating large-scale mining and analysis tasks (intended for SLURM or similar batch systems).

        • 01_initial_information_miner.sh: Gathers initial repository and project metadata.
        • 02_github_miner.sh: Mines commit and issue data from GitHub repositories.
        • 02_jira_issue_miner.sh: Extracts issue tracking data from JIRA.
        • 03_match_issue_data.sh: Matches mined issue data with corresponding commits.
        • 04_projects_summary.sh: Generates a summary of all processed projects.
        • ck.sh: Runs the CK Java metrics analyzer.
        • jasome.sh: Executes Jasome for code metric extraction.
        • pmd.sh: Runs PMD static analysis tool to extract defect metrics.
        • rminer.sh: Executes RefactoringMiner to detect code refactorings.
        • pp_rminer.sh: Runs RefactoringMiner++ (for C++ or multi-language analysis).
        • py_rminer.sh: Executes Python RefactoringMiner.
        • sq.sh: Runs SonarQube analysis.
        • und.sh: Runs SciTools Understand for static code metrics.

      • scripts/: Python scripts organized by tool and functionality.

        • commons.py: Contains shared constants, paths, and helper functions used across the workflow.
        • codescene/: Scripts for running CodeScene analysis.
          • run_cs.py: Executes CodeScene tool and handles its output.
        • sq/: Scripts related to SonarQube execution.
          • run_sq.py: Runs SonarQube analysis and exports results.
        • understand/: Scripts related to SciTools Understand.
          • run_understand.py: Automates Understand analysis and result collection.
        • rminer/: Scripts for RefactoringMiner.
          • run_rminer.py: Runs RefactoringMiner to detect refactoring operations.
        • py_rminer/: Scripts for Python RefactoringMiner.
          • run_py_rminer.py: Executes the Python-specific RefactoringMiner version.
        • rminer_pp/: Scripts for RefactoringMiner++.
          • run_pp_rminer.py: Runs the extended RefactoringMiner++ analysis.
        • ck/: Scripts for running CK metric extraction.
          • run_ck.py: Executes CK Java metrics collection.
        • pmd/: Scripts for running PMD analysis.
          • run_pmd.py: Runs PMD for detecting defects and code smells.
        • jasome/: Scripts for Jasome metric analysis.
          • run_jasome.py: Executes Jasome to extract object-oriented metrics.
        • main_workflow/: Orchestrates the overall multi-tool mining pipeline.
          • 01_initial_information_miner.py: Collects initial metadata for repositories and releases.
          • 02_github_miner.py: Mines GitHub data such as commits, contributors, and issues.
          • 02_jira_miner.py: Mines JIRA issue tracking data.
          • 02_bugzilla_miner.py: Extracts issues from Bugzilla trackers.
          • 03_match_issue_data.py: Matches commits with corresponding issue records.
          • 04_projects_summary_table.py: Creates per-project summaries combining mined data.
          • 05_merge_summaries.py: Aggregates all per-project summaries into a cross-project dataset.

      • config_files/: Contains SLURM configuration files for executing different parts of the mining pipeline.

        • config.srun: Main SLURM job configuration for the pipeline.
        • config_jasome.srun: Configuration file for running Jasome analyses.
        • config_und.srun: Configuration for SciTools Understand jobs.

    • database_generation/: Contains all scripts and files to initialize the database and prepare schema definitions for storing mined data.

      • createTables.py: Python script that defines SQL table creation logic for repository and metric storage.
      • map.json: Mapping configuration file linking schema attributes or data source columns.
      • create.sql: SQL script containing DDL statements for database initialization.
      • final_csv_headers.txt: Defines the standardized CSV header fields used across merged datasets.

    • result_merge/: Main directory for merging, integrating, and enriching mined datasets from different tools.

      • batch_jobs/: Contains shell scripts automating data merging and post-processing.

        • merge_batch_results.sh: Merges partial batch analysis results into a global dataset.
        • rminer_csv_generator.sh: Generates CSVs from RefactoringMiner outputs.
        • issue_csv_generator.sh: Converts issue-tracking system data into unified CSVs.
        • sq_csv_generator.sh: Processes SonarQube metrics.
        • codescene_csv_generator.sh: Aggregates CodeScene analysis outputs.
        • pyref_csv_generator.sh: Handles Python RefactoringMiner results.
        • und_csv_generator.sh: Converts SciTools Understand outputs to CSV format.
        • merge_process_metrics.sh: Merges process and activity metrics.
        • pmd_csv_generator.sh: Extracts and merges PMD metrics.
        • merge_github_metrics.sh: Combines GitHub repository-level metadata.
        • check_completeness.sh: Verifies dataset completeness and consistency.
        • map_vulnerability_issues.sh: Maps vulnerability-related issues (CVEs) to commit data.
        • interealease_process_metrics.sh: Calculates inter-release process metrics.
        • jasome_csv_generator.sh: Generates metrics CSVs from Jasome XML output.
        • pp_rminer_csv_generator.sh: Processes RefactoringMiner++ results.
        • ck_csv_generator.sh: Converts CK Java metrics to CSV.
        • enrich_release_data.sh: Enriches release-level data with extra metrics and context.

      • scripts/: Python scripts implementing data merging, enrichment, and validation logic.

        • check_completeness_01.py: Performs dataset completeness verification.
        • merge_batch_results_02.py: Merges batch job results across multiple projects.
        • pmd_global_csv_generator_03.py: Aggregates PMD metrics globally.
        • ck_global_csv_generator_04.py: Consolidates CK metrics from all projects.
        • jasome_global_csv_generator_05.py: Processes Jasome output for all releases.
        • rminer_global_csv_generator_06.py: Generates global CSVs from RefactoringMiner data.
        • release_global_metrics_07.py: Computes release-level aggregated metrics.
        • map_vulnerability_issues_08.py: Links mined commits to known vulnerabilities.
        • enrich_release_data_09.py: Enriches releases with issue and commit metadata.
        • issue_csv_generator_10.py: Generates issue-tracking CSVs for JIRA, GitHub, etc.
        • get_cwe_documentation_11.py: Retrieves CWE documentation details.
        • get_cve_documentation_12.py: Downloads and integrates CVE vulnerability metadata.
        • merge_all_issue_data_13.py: Integrates all issue datasets into one unified structure.
        • merge_all_commit_data_14.py: Aggregates all commit-related datasets.
        • sq_global_csv_generator_15.py: Collects SonarQube results globally.
        • und_global_csv_generator_16.py: Merges Understand static analysis results.
        • codescene_global_csv_generator_17.py: Aggregates CodeScene project-level data.
        • pyref_global_csv_generator_18.py: Processes Python RefactoringMiner (PyRef) outputs.
        • rminerpp_global_csv_generator_19.py: Handles RefactoringMiner++ results at global scale.
        • create_final_releases_table_20.py: Builds a final releases table joining all project datasets.
        • merge_vulnerability_measures_21.py: Merges vulnerability-related metrics into the dataset.
        • merge_github_metrics_22.py: Combines GitHub metadata (stars, forks, etc.).
        • merge_process_metrics_23.py: Final merge step for all process-related metrics.
        • utils.py: Utility functions shared across scripts.

License

All generated data is released under the Creative Commons 4.0 Attribution License (CC BY 4.0).

All scripts are provided under the MIT License.

All the analysed projects must be used in accordance with their respective licenses (shared in each project when applicable).

Running the code

This project msr-dataset is composed of two main repositories — tool_mining and result_merge — which together form the complete mining and integration pipeline.
All analyses are performed through SLURM-based batch execution, and the order of execution strictly follows the numbering in the Python script filenames (e.g., _01, _02, _03, etc.).

⚙️ 1. Path Configuration

Before running any scripts, the practitioner must configure machine-specific paths.

📌 Files to Update

Repository File Description
result_merge result_merge/scripts/utils.py Update base directories and paths according to your system.
tool_mining scripts/commons.py Set correct absolute paths for repositories, datasets, and output directories.

In addition, all SLURM batch (.sh) and configuration (.srun) filesmust have their internal paths updated to reflect your local environment (e.g., project directories, conda environments, scratch paths).
There is no need to modify paths inside Python scripts — these are handled automatically via the configuration utilities mentioned above.

🚀 2. Execution Order and Workflow

Each numbered script or batch file corresponds to a specific stage in the mining or integration pipeline.
Always execute the scripts incrementally, respecting their numeric prefixes.

🧩 Step-by-Step Workflow

Phase 1: Repository and Issue Mining (msr-dataset/tool_mining/)

Each Python script in msr-dataset/tool_mining/scripts/main_workflow has a corresponding SLURM batch job in msr-dataset/tool_mining/batch_jobs.
Run each step through its respective .sh file, incrementally:

  1. 01_initial_information_miner.sh → Initializes project and repository metadata.
  2. 02_github_miner.sh, 02_jira_issue_miner.sh, 02_bugzilla_miner.sh → Mines commit and issue data from different sources.
  3. 03_match_issue_data.sh → Links mined issues with commit data.
  4. 04_projects_summary.sh → Generates per-project summaries.
  5. Execute additional analysis tools:
    • rminer.sh, pp_rminer.sh, py_rminer.sh → Run RefactoringMiner / RefactoringMiner++ / PyRef.
    • jasome.sh, ck.sh, pmd.sh, sq.sh, und.sh → Run metric-based analysis (Jasome, CK, PMD, SonarQube, Understand).
Phase 2: Data Integration and Merging (msr-dataset/result_merge)

Once all tool outputs are generated, execute the scripts inside msr-dataset/result_merge/scripts in incremental order using their respective SLURM .sh jobs under msr-dataset/result_merge/batch_jobs.

Example execution sequence:

  1. check_completeness_01.py → Validate dataset completeness.
  2. merge_batch_results_02.py → Merge initial batch outputs.
  3. pmd_global_csv_generator_03.py, ck_global_csv_generator_04.py, etc. → Aggregate tool-specific results.
  4. Continue incrementally through to merge_process_metrics_23.py— the final data integration step.

Each of these Python scripts is intended to be executed through its related .sh job file (e.g., pmd_csv_generator.sh for PMD data).

3. Execution Command Example

All scripts are executed using SLURM via the sbatch command:

```bash
sbatch batch_jobs/01_initial_information_miner.sh
sbatch batch_jobs/02_github_miner.sh
sbatch batch_jobs/03_match_issue_data.sh
...
sbatch batch_jobs/04_projects_summary.sh

metadata.title: INTERADIG analysis code and documentation (no participant data)
metadata.description:
Overview: Public replication package for the INTERADIG real-world study of telephone/SMS support for a prescription digital therapeutic in Germany (DiGA context). This record contains the analysis code (SPSS v30) and the variable codebook used to generate the manuscript’s results.

Important: No participant-level data are included. The microdata are owned by the provider and are available under restricted access in a companion Zenodo record (see Related works).

Contents:
• MA2_INTERADIG_Analysis.pdf: end-to-end SPSS syntax (v30 compatible)
• MA1_Codebook.pdf: variable names, labels, codings, and derived measures
• README.pdf: how to run and reproduce outputs

How to reproduce: Load your analysis dataset as the active file, then run SPSS syntax from top to bottom. The script computes adherence metrics (v1/v2), domain goal attainment, reactivation after inactivity, survival (time-to-first inactivity), non-responder checks, and adjusted outcome models (IIEF-5, CGI-I), matching the manuscript.

License: CC BY 4.0 for code and documentation. Cite this record and the article when reusing.

Contact: For questions or to request access to the restricted microdata, please contact the corresponding author.

metadata.description:
ARG-V Replication Package

This record serves as a guide to the purpose of each component of this package, as well as information for reproducing the results of the ARG-V transformer and our experiments in the paper Demonstrating ARG-V ’s Generation of Realistic Java Benchmarks for SV-COMP.

This artifact contains two major and distinct components: `argv-transformer` itself and the experiments run comparing benchmarks produced by the transformer and the existing SV-COMP benchmark corpus. The paper revolves primarily around demonstrating ARG-V's capability to produce benchmarks that provide ample challenge for the state of the art in Java verifiers, so we have included a comprehensive script for fully replicating our experiments on your own machine.

NOTE: This replication requires x86/amd64 to run. It will NOT run on ARM (Mac).

UPDATE: The instructions include text about extracting the Zip file to “/home/argv”.  This is an incorrect path.  It should be “/home/tacas/argv” instead.  All commands should be run from that directory.
